messages:
arjun: Quick sync — planning a cross-bench for SmoothQuant + activation-aware quant on longspan workloads. Aim: compare AWQ, GPTQ, FP8 mixed, and our SmoothQuant+act-aware pipeline across 64k/96k/128k profiles.

maria: I kicked off the first sweep this morning on a 4-gpu dedicated pool. Workloads: longbench-v2 chat, doc-retrieval traces, and synthetic long-span summarization.

ben: Nice. What configs? can you paste the run command?

maria: Sure — here's the launcher we used:

```
./run_bakeoff --model raven-13b --quant-pipelines awq,gptq,fp8,smooth+actaware 
  --seq-lens 65536,98304,131072 
  --batch 1 --kv-cache true --warmup 200 --tokens 200k 
  --eval-set longbench-v2 --seed 42
```

sylvia: Did you enable per-layer act smoothing? any per-layer clamp params?

maria: Enabled smooth factor=0.9 global, per-layer clamp thresholds auto-calibrated from calibration set. Also tried a hand-tuned run with clamp=[0.95,0.9,0.85] for early/mid/late layers.

arjun: Good — keep the calibration artifacts. We need the exact accuracy deltas per pipeline and perf profiles (p50/p95 latency, tokens/sec, KV hit ratios). Also failure modes: hallucination spikes and temperature sensitivity.

ben: Early results (summary):
- GPTQ baseline: highest geom accuracy but 3.2x slower at 128k due to KV eviction churn. p95 1140ms (128k), tokens/sec 18.
- AWQ (default): smoother perf, tokens/sec 26 at 128k, but EM delta -2.4% on longbench QA compared to FP32.
- FP8-mix (per-layer): tokens/sec 31 at 128k, p95 720ms, but rare outlier decoding drift on summarization tasks.
- SmoothQuant+act-aware: tokens/sec 29, p95 760ms, EM delta -0.8% and much lower tail-regressions on our evals.

maria: Adding the micro metrics — KV cache retention dropped ~14% for GPTQ at 128k; Smooth+act-aware retained ~94% KV hits vs 97% for FP32.

sylvia: Interesting that FP8 was fastest but had drift. Do we have loss curves or sample-wise divergence logs?

maria: Yup — attached calibration logs on GCS, sample diffs flagged where token-level KL > 0.6. Most FP8 drifts in low-prob tokens during abstractive summarization.

arjun: For rollout policy: propose canary for Smooth+act-aware on dedicated first, with fallback to FP32/GPTQ combo. Must include per-route latency SLOs and an auto-fallback when sample divergence > threshold for X consecutive requests.

ben: Agreed. Also add a quality monitor check: rolling window 10k tokens, trigger when EM delta > 1.5% or KL spikes > 0.5.

maria: Will create canary job configs. Example deploy snippet:

```
route: /v1/generate/longspan
model_variant: raven-13b-sq-actaware-qa
canary: 5%
fallbacks: [raven-13b-gptq, raven-13b-fp32]
quality_monitors:
  - name: em-delta
    window: 10000
    threshold: 0.015
  - name: kl-token
    window: 5000
    threshold: 0.5
```

sylvia: One more ask — can you run a short resilience test: simulate KV eviction and spike inflight requests to see degradation curve? We care about graceful degradation.

maria: On it. Scheduling a 2h resilience sweep tonight (will post results).

eva-ci-bot: build 2026.3.4 passed for bakeoff harness; artifacts: gs://redwood-bench/2138723456/run-2026-03-20.tar.gz

arjun: Cool. Once resilience numbers are in, we can pick the default canary config and prepare release notes. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:

ben: If SmoothQuant+act-aware keeps <1% EM delta and p95 < 800ms at 128k, I'm +1 for dedicated canary.

sylvia: Also schedule an eval on our internal safety prompts — want to ensure quantization doesn't increase unsafe completions.

maria: Will append that to the sweep. Posting initial numeric tables and logs after the resilience run completes.

arjun: Perfect. Let's reconvene tomorrow after artifacts are uploaded.
